main_text.head: LECTURO, S.
main_text.p: {R}EM publico nec ingratam nec inutilem nos facturos, visum est, si hasce de operationibus Dæmonum dissertationes secunda vice in publicum edi accuraremus. Fervet hoc tempore, occasione libri cujusdam belgice à viro docto confcripti, hæc quæstio. Eo de libro arbitrari nostri judicii res haut est. Has tantum tecum communicamus dissertationes, idque duplici potissimum nomine, cum ut eæ-dem fili sint tibi loco, quo errabun-da vestigia regas, quodque in ipsa a-dyta hujus litis te ducat, tum maxi-me ut constet, quam longe Philoso-phiæ Cartefianæ Σλοιχεῖα remota sint à fundamentis, quibus suum ædificium libri Belgici autor super-struit, & quam iniqui rerum arbitri sint ii, qui in triviis, in compitis, & ubi non, imperito vulgo persuadere sum-

page.notes: The woodcut initial R is joined to the first word; it is rendered as "REM" with the initial letter in braces only as a marker of the decorated letter. The first word reads "Em" with the initial R: likely "Rem" (initial R, then "em"). Line-end hyphen in "con-" and "communica-" kept as printed. Page continues in part 2. Part 2 of a page; the top of the column is cut off. The catchword "sum-" is printed at the right below the last line. The Greek word Σλοιχεῖα is as printed (στοιχεῖα). Some letters in the lower lines are blurred ("ubi non" and "suum") and may be misread.
